title: Forward light moves at $c$, backward light at $2v - c$

statements.text: Under the emission rule, forward light moves at $v + (c - v) = c$ in the absolute frame and backward light at $v - (c - v) = 2v - c$. Below $v = c/2$ backward light moves backward at $c - 2v$, at $v = c/2$ it stands still, and above it even backward light moves forward.

sources.quote: Below v = c/2, backward-emitted light travels backwards at speed c − 2v.
At v = c/2, it is stationary in the absolute frame.
